title: The shared guard core reads the ruling store before any refusal: a ruled lift lets the act through and names the ruling
why: R59 part 3 (owner 15:05 CST Nov 12: "ruling governs the guard right away"; plan 9064e3c1; store roadmap/rulings/r59.json). Owner 15:11 CST: "guards that trigger off main's code that give feeedback to sessions i wonder if sessions will then remember that the store supercedes them". The refusal tells the session, so it never has to remember (retrospective 15:12 CST).
source: retrospective 15:12 CST Nov 12, under R59 part 3
note: Lane ruled-store-one-home builds only the lookup (lint/ruled_store.py ruling_for_guard, guard_ruling_line). This step: (1) wires that lookup into the shared guard core, one home, before any refusal; (2) when an open, checked entry lifts the rule, the act goes through and prints "allowed by ruling <id>"; (3) when an entry names the rule without lifting it, the refusal adds "a newer ruling may apply: <id>, <title>"; (4) adds one CLAUDE.md line: an open, checked entry outranks main's text. Red first on a guard refusal with a lifting entry. A guard verdict change: round 3 gets the net-value test. Express (R55). Part 5 (retrospective 15:13 CST Nov 12; owner 15:13 CST: "will the guards that are ai driven then also pull the store so they won't be rotten with just main's rules and instead have the newer prose too"): read, only call_judge.py and question_form.py use past_ruling_context; prose_judge, reply_judge, the feedback_guard repeat judge and decision_watch build their own context from main. Extend past_ruling_context in call_judge.py (one home, no second helper) to give every model-judged guard the open, checked store entries that touch what it judges, each marked as outranking main's text; every judge calls it. Cost: one read of the local roadmap ref per judge call, no fetch, no new process. A test proves a judge sees an entry that contradicts main's text and follows the entry. Sighting 15:53 CST Nov 12: the page write of item 651 passed the past-ruling hook though fix-check-after-main-merge (R1) already ruled it; only the report-time guard caught it.
